items.text: Optimize session dropdown

thread.text: Analyzing this item and researching the codebase...

Research complete. Three concrete optimization targets found: (1) Every dropdown open fires TWO round-trips — a GET /sessions?limit=50 (even though the list is already rendered from cache) plus a POST /sessions/refresh that is a no-op returning changed:false outside hybrid mode. The 15s poll already keeps the cache fresh, so opens are doing redundant work. (2) Keyboard support stops at the trigger: Enter/Space toggles and Escape closes, but rows aren't focusable and there's no arrow navigation — switching sessions is mouse-only. (3) The 50-row cap is hard-coded in the fetch URL AND enforced server-side (limit le=50); pinned sessions always show, so only older unpinned ones get trimmed, and sessions beyond 50 are unreachable from the dropdown (the Sessions page has them). Before proposing a plan, three questions: 1) What motivated this item — slow open, keyboard-only switching, finding sessions past the cap, or all of it? 2) For keyboard work: arrows + Home/End + Enter-to-switch (plus type-ahead) acceptable, with the full search-bar footer left to the separate related item? 3) Keep the 50-row cap, or add a load-more/pagination path so older sessions stay reachable?

qa.research_notes: ui/chat/js/session-list.js renders rows (pin, family carets, status, kebab/trash) and fetches via /api/v1/db/sessions?limit=50 (+ include_hidden). ui/chat/js/session-init.js owns open/close: _loadSessionList() calls populateSessionSelect() (GET) + refreshSessionMetadata() (POST /sessions/refresh) on EVERY open. Keyboard handling exists only on the trigger (Enter/Space toggle, Escape close) — no arrow navigation over rows. The 50-row cap is hard-coded in the fetch URL. Sessions Page (ui/main-panel/sessions) has the full list + recycle bin + restore, so the dropdown is the quick-switch surface. POST /sessions/refresh is a hybrid-mirror sync (app/api/db_viewer.py:473) that returns {"changed":false} immediately when no hybrid backend is configured — a wasted round-trip on every open in the default local setup. The server enforces limit le=50 (app/api/db_viewer.py list_sessions); pinned sessions are fetched without a limit, so only older unpinned sessions are trimmed. refreshSessionMetadata() refetches only when changed; the 15s poll (menu closed, session-init.js:1342) already keeps _sessionsCache fresh, so the GET on open is largely redundant.

Three questions posted.

→ Yes all sessions and content. It needs to mimic the session page search

Q2) When a search query is active, should recycled matches appear automatically (with a 'bin' badge, like the Sessions page cross-catalog search), or only when the recycle-bin toggle is on?
→ Yes there should be a bin flag and click to restore just like session page

Q3) In recycle-bin mode, how should restoring work: a per-row restore button, click-the-row-to-restore, or a two-click confirm like the Sessions page?

thread.text: Analyzing this item and researching the codebase...

Research complete. The mic button (#chat-voice-btn) is rendered unconditionally via the mic_send control in chat_ui.json; support is only checked on click inside startSpeechDictation (native SpeechRecognition, or MediaRecorder + getUserMedia with server LLM transcription, per the /api/v1/auth/ui-config voice policy). On unsupported browsers the button still shows and just pops an error alert — this item reverses that. A ready-made hook exists: the .no-voice pill class (used by the web-chat sign-in gate) already hides the mic and forces send-only. Two questions before the plan:

Q1) Should the mic hide only in the main chat composer, or also in the other places it appears (Gen UI page toolbar, app-config assistant, secondary search pills)?
→ it should hide everywhere where browser mic is not supported

Q2) On non-HTTPS addresses (e.g. LAN over http) the mic APIs are unavailable — hide the button there too, or keep showing it with the existing ‘requires HTTPS’ alert on click?
→ yes hide it there too

Plan ready. Hide the mic everywhere voice input is unsupported (no SpeechRecognition AND no MediaRecorder+getUserMedia, or a non-secure context) via one shared isVoiceInputSupported() in attachments.js applied at every mic-button wiring site — the main composer reuses the existing .no-voice CSS hook to go send-only; Gen UI pill, app-config assistant and secondary pills hide the button directly. Review the plan to start the change.

Done — implemented. isVoiceInputSupported() in ui/shared/js/attachments.js now gates every mic button: the main composer (#chat-input-row), Gen UI page pill and ability-search pill go send-only via the existing .no-voice CSS hook; the app-config assistant and the legacy voice element hide the button directly; forwardChatPillControls never forwards to a hidden mic. Covers non-HTTPS and unsupported browsers (no SpeechRecognition AND no MediaRecorder), plus an async refinement that hides the mic when LLM dictation is disabled and there is no native SpeechRecognition. All five edited files pass node --check.

thread.text: Analyzing this item and researching the codebase...

Root cause found. The handle (#chat-footer-handle) and its CSS both exist and nothing clips them, but the JS visibility checks keep hiding it. Two checks decide visibility: _updateFooterHandleVisibility() in ui/chat/js/chat-ui.js and the checks in ui/chat-controls/chat-controls-config.js (_buildActiveFooter + switchFooterMode active branch). All three only inspect DIRECT children of #chat-footer-row for the data-header-control attribute. Since the row-layout refactor, footer buttons live nested inside generated .chat-header-row[data-controls-row] > .chat-header-zone > button — so they are never direct children — and manifest-driven controls like wake_lock carry data-element-origin instead of data-header-control. The check always evaluates false, the handle gets display:none, and the drag/click toggle is dead. Fix: query descendants via r.querySelectorAll('[data-header-control], [data-element-origin]') in all three spots. Plan proposed — review it to start the change.

Done. findings: Automatic Source Control refreshes launch expensive remote Git fetch/status/graph work while ordinary chat and session reads are active.

The diagnostics recorder performs its first prune three seconds after startup. Its 331 MB logs.db cleanup used synchronous SQLite DELETE/ORDER BY/commit operations directly inside an async coroutine.

findings: The Chat toggle is synchronous DOM work; the long click was an app-wide event-loop/I/O contention symptom, not a blocking click handler.

changesValidated: Cached memory or IndexedDB rows now paint before server verification and remain usable under a visible Syncing state.

IndexedDB honors pinned sort_order including zero, sorts unpinned rows by real activity, and applies drag order atomically before server acknowledgement with reconcile-or-rollback on failure.
Hidden or collapsed Chat pauses idle tail, session-list and related-session polling; slow list polls cannot overlap their next interval.
Session-tail database routing uses a bounded TTL cache, removing the redundant hot-path SQLite open while avoiding caching transient failures.

Estimated and provider-reported actual costs are exposed for each guest and its shared network.
Actual network cost exhaustion stops the agent at the next model-call boundary and refuses later admissions.
Anonymous rows compute proximity from guest and network token/cost metrics and sort closest-to-limit first.
Registered traffic remains outside anonymous network buckets and continues on account credits and tier.
limitations: The isolated browser was correctly anonymous, so the admin-only Instances > Users visual checkpoint was blocked rather than bypassed.
The first browser chat was accepted and visibly acknowledged; complete assistant-response quality was not part of this allowance run.

Server evidence captured a non-blocking 500 from the anonymous current-model-info probe; chat still completed and browser console warning/error output was empty, so this remains a separate regression to diagnose.
runs.next: Repeat the operator visual checkpoint in an authenticated disposable admin profile and calibrate the conservative per-turn estimate against production model prices.

researchNotes.edgeStrategy: Use progressive challenge, bot scoring and multi-characteristic counting at the edge; always validate challenge tokens server-side. Keep origin global breakers even after WAF deployment.
researchNotes.privacy: Network prefixes, TLS fingerprints, bot scores and behavioral similarity are risk signals, not identity proof. Use keyed/rotating pseudonyms, short retention, preview mode and a registration escape hatch for shared networks.

projects.name: Manager Parallel Mini-Loops
projects.info: Four bounded Manager mini-loops supervise the main agent loop without replacing its mechanical contracts. Plan, edit, and commit gates can be advisory (async) or blocking; the watchdog is always async. All triggers are opt-in per agent, independently gated by the manager_chk loop node and the live run_manager app-function toggle.

items.text: Validate Manager configuration, verdict contracts, prompt fallback, and active-run feedback formatting (11/11 passed).
Validate exact A/B oscillation detection, changing-argument false-positive avoidance, error windows, and cooldown (3/3 passed).
Validate overall/per-kind caps and one shared retry timeout budget (3/3 passed).
Run the complete focused Manager/guardrail regression suite (41/41 passed).
Document all trigger points, blocking/advisory modes, evidence contracts, and default limits.
Exercise a real disposable chat run with deterministic Manager verdicts and capture pipeline events.
Prove system:manager persistence, next-inference injection, and reload behavior from UI/API/database evidence.
Prove three consecutive blocking verdicts emit manager_escalation_stop and prevent further tool execution.

featureTest.description: Validate the Manager as four parallel supervisory mini-loops around the main agent loop. The main loop first applies deterministic validation, contract, loop, and user-confirmation checks. Only otherwise-valid actions reach Manager gates. Async reviews run beside the main loop and inject actionable advice at the next inference boundary; blocking reviews await a bounded verdict and fail open on Manager error or timeout.

triggerMap.trigger: First otherwise-valid edit/write tool request in a run
triggerMap.gate: Runs after mechanical validation/contracts/confirmation. Blocking mode must approve before the edit proceeds; async mode advises the next inference.
Judges the specific tool name and arguments against the request/working plan. Blocking verdicts prevent that edit.

triggerMap.trigger: Periodic every_n_turns or structured run-health event
triggerMap.gate: Always advisory. Health inputs include identical calls, exact A/B oscillation, same-result/no-progress loops, tool budgets, validation/contract/guardrail/Manager failures, and sliding-window tool errors.
Receives intended commit arguments, changed paths/edit inventory, and verification summary only. Blocking mode can prevent commit/push; async mode does not delay it.

masterGates.manager_chk: Independent loop node for all Manager LLM checks.
masterGates.contract_chk: Separate deterministic contract node; not replaced by Manager.

max_blocks.meaning: Consecutive blocking/revise verdicts before safe escalation stop; blocking approvals reset the count.

timeout_seconds.meaning: One total deadline shared by both LLM attempts; Manager failure is fail-open.

watchdog.every_n_turns: Periodic advisory cadence; 0 disables periodic checks.
watchdog.on_errors: Failures required inside error_window; 0 disables error-cluster checks.
watchdog.error_window: Sliding outcome window; default 8 and never below on_errors.
watchdog.on_stall: Enables structured stall/loop/guard health triggers; default true when watchdog object is used.
watchdog.cooldown_turns: Minimum turns between watchdog launches; default 2.

parameters.verdictContract: Every verdict requires non-empty reason. revise/block require feedback; off_track/stuck require suggestion. Invalid responses retry within the shared deadline, then fail open.

testCases.title: Gate modes and verdict contracts
steps: Resolve default and overridden Manager metadata and observe normalized gate modes/caps.
Parse valid and malformed kind-specific verdicts and observe strict required fields.
Format actionable feedback and a bad custom prompt fallback and observe kind-correct output.
testCases.expected: Only valid verdicts become Manager decisions; each trigger remains opt-in and independently configured.

testCases.title: Watchdog health signals
steps: Feed exact canonical A/B/A/B/A/B requests and observe one alternating_tool_loop event.
Change arguments across the same tool-name sequence and observe no false positive.
Feed failure/success/failure/failure into a four-result window and observe threshold plus cooldown behavior.
testCases.expected: Only evidence-backed stalls trigger a bounded async watchdog review.

testCases.title: Budgets and fail-open timeout
steps: Attempt a check beyond max_checks and observe no Manager call.
Attempt a watchdog check beyond its kind cap and observe no Manager call.
Make the first LLM attempt consume the test deadline and observe no second full timeout.
testCases.expected: Manager work is bounded per lane and overall and cannot freeze the main loop.

testCases.title: Blocking gates and safe escalation in a disposable run
steps: Start a controlled disposable agent with blocking plan/edit/commit gates.
Return approve, revise, and three consecutive block verdicts from the deterministic provider.
Observe allowed actions, blocked actions, block-count reset, manager_escalation_stop, and no later tool execution.
testCases.expected: Blocking gates govern only their guarded action and repeated Manager blocks end safely.

testCases.title: Active feedback, persistence, usage, and reload
steps: Delay an async off_track verdict until a tool completes.
Observe one Manager system message in the next provider request and one system:manager row.
Reload the chat and compare UI, API/database row, usage manager:<kind> entry, console, and HTTP evidence.
testCases.expected: Advice reaches the active run exactly once, remains durable, and does not duplicate after reload.

qa.testTemplate:
[Project Readiness Agent — TEST ITEM]
Project: ${project} (${status})
Feature to validate: ${item} [test]
QA Status: ${qaStatus}
User Hint: ${hint}
--- Q&A Thread ---
${thread}
${action}

ROLE: This is a TEST item, not a development task. Your job is to VALIDATE the described feature — do NOT fix, implement, or modify any code. The feature description may need sharpening; if it is not specific enough to test, ask clarifying questions first (QUESTION RULES apply — do not propose a plan while questions are pending).

PHASE 1 — TEST PLAN (do this first, never skip): Write a thorough, precise description of the feature and the tests that prove it works, into qa.plan:
- approach: the full feature description — what the feature must do, its inputs and outputs, and the edge cases it must handle
- files: the components/areas under test (file paths or UI surfaces)
- steps: concrete test steps, each stating the action AND the expected result (the acceptance criteria)
- effort/impact/risks: as usual
Set qa.status to plan_ready and refresh the genui. Do NOT execute any test yet.

PHASE 2 — EXECUTION: Only after the user accepts the plan, RUN the tests against the live app — browser interactions, API calls, code inspection, or any other non-mutating verification. Record each test in qa.execution_log with status done (PASS) or error (FAIL/BLOCKED), detail naming the actual vs expected outcome, and refresh the genui as you go. Never modify source files — this is validation only. When all tests are complete, append a final entry: All tests complete — N passed, M failed/blocked.
